children: , the e-commerce, advertising and cloud-computing powerhouse, tumbled approximately 4.6% to $254.18 Tuesday as regulators went straight for its advertising machine. The Federal Trade Commission and 22 states allege Amazon rigged sponsored-product auctions and extracted more than $20 billion from over one million sellers and brands.

The FTC complaint claims Amazon changed the rules in 2019 and later interfered in as many as 80% of sponsored-product auctions. Amazon fired back, saying average winning bids fell 50% between 2019 and 2025. It also argues that the system saved advertisers roughly $8 billion.

This is not a sideshow. Advertising delivered $19.8 billion of revenue last quarter, surged 26% and accounted for nearly 10% of Amazon's total sales. The picture adds another pressure point: at $254.18, the stock trades 2.83% above its $247.18 GF Value estimate, leaving little valuation cushion while regulators attack the economics behind one of Amazon's fastest-growing businesses.

title: Amazon Stock Drops 4.6% as FTC Alleges More Than $20 Billion in Ad Overcharges
